caseStudies.title: Swiggy Instamart UX Overhaul
caseStudies.subtitle: 10-Minute Grocery — Zero-Friction Checkout
caseStudies.tagline: Speed is the feature. Every tap that slows you down is a broken promise.
caseStudies.summary: A ground-up UX audit and redesign of the Swiggy Instamart checkout flow — reducing friction from cart to confirmation by eliminating redundant steps and surfacing trust signals at the right moments.
caseStudies.detTagline: Speed is the feature. Every tap that slows you down is a broken promise.
caseStudies.detBrief: Swiggy Instamart promises 10-minute delivery, but the checkout flow — riddled with address re-confirmation loops, buried coupons, and a multi-step payment wall — consistently undermined that promise. The goal was to redesign the end-to-end cart-to-confirmation journey so that it felt as fast as the delivery itself, without sacrificing clarity or trust.
caseStudies.detThinking: I started with a heuristic audit of the existing flow, mapping every screen against Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics. Three anti-patterns surfaced immediately: forced re-entry of delivery slot even when the default was valid, coupon discovery buried three taps deep, and a payment confirmation page that offered no reassurance before charging. From there I ran 6 moderated usability sessions (3 frequent users, 3 occasional), coded the sessions for task failure and hesitation moments, and built an affinity map in Miro. The redesign centred on three principles — progressive disclosure, persistent context (showing delivery ETA at every step), and a single-screen payment summary that collapsed address, slot, and payment into one scannable view.
caseStudies.detMyRole: Solo project — conducted all research (heuristic audit + usability sessions), synthesised findings, defined the redesign scope, created all wireframes (lo-fi → hi-fi) in Figma, built an interactive prototype and ran a second round of unmoderated testing via Maze to validate the redesigned flow against the original.
caseStudies.detOutcome: Task completion on the redesigned prototype was 94% vs 71% on the original flow (n=18, Maze). Time-to-payment dropped by an average of 38 seconds. All 6 usability participants rated the redesigned confirmation screen as more trustworthy. The project is currently being used as a portfolio piece and is under review for a potential internship engagement.

caseStudies.title: Namisite Admin Dashboard
caseStudies.subtitle: Internal Tool Design & Prototype
caseStudies.tagline: A dashboard should answer your questions before you think to ask them.
caseStudies.summary: Designed a data-dense internal admin dashboard for Namisite's ops team — balancing information density with clarity to let admins manage clients, track activity, and action alerts without switching contexts.
caseStudies.detTagline: A dashboard should answer your questions before you think to ask them.
caseStudies.detBrief: The Namisite ops team was managing client accounts across three separate spreadsheets and a legacy CRM. Errors were slipping through. The brief was to design a unified admin dashboard that would give the team a single source of truth for client status, recent activity, and pending actions — all within a clean, low-latency interface.
caseStudies.detThinking: I spent the first week shadowing two ops team members to map their actual workflow — not what they said they did, but what they actually did. The big insight: 80% of daily admin work boiled down to three questions — who needs attention right now, what changed since yesterday, and where is my team stuck. The design response was a priority-first layout: a triage column of flagged items on the left, a live activity feed in the centre, and a client detail panel that slid in without a page load on the right. I used FigJam to workshop the IA with the team before a single frame was opened in Figma.
caseStudies.detMyRole: Led the end-to-end design process — stakeholder interviews, workflow mapping, information architecture, lo-fi wireframes, design system setup (tokens, components), hi-fi UI, and a clickable Figma prototype used in two rounds of internal testing.
caseStudies.detOutcome: The prototype was signed off after two feedback rounds with zero major structural changes — a first for this client. The engineering team began implementation in Q2 2026. Formal metrics pending post-launch.
